mission.name: XRP intelligence and prediction-engine mastery
mission.foundation: Barrot V3 execution, orchestration, safety and verification

source_capture_policy.timestamp_anchor: web retrieval time from current session; no independent external timestamp anchor
source_capture_policy.admission_rule: Keep this qualitative institutional event outside the prediction feature store until byte-complete source captures, hashes, publication vintages and independent timestamps are stored.

claims_supported: BNY states that its Digital Asset Custody platform now supports native XRP and RLUSD for eligible institutional clients.
BNY describes eligible-client safekeeping, holding and transfer capability.
BNY intends to broaden XRPL tokenized-asset support and enable direct RLUSD mint/redeem through BNY, subject to final BNY and regulatory approvals.
BNY and Ripple describe exploring tokenized trade finance on XRPL with C2FO, subject to client requirements.
limitations: BNY reports capability, not asset-specific XRP or RLUSD assets under custody, client counts, account openings or incremental purchases.
Direct RLUSD mint/redeem is an intended future product plan, not verified production service.
Tokenized trade finance is exploratory; no funded receivables, investor allocations or production settlement volumes are disclosed.

claims_supported: C2FO Instant Pay financing and settlement activity is intended to use XRPL.
The named settlement asset is RLUSD.
The announced funding model uses participating capital providers to fund accelerated supplier payments against approved invoices.
Suppliers are described as receiving funds in seconds rather than days, while invoice terms and due dates remain unchanged.
The announcement directs interested businesses to a waitlist.
limitations: The release announces an initiative; it does not identify the participating capital providers or disclose funded amounts, supplier counts or production throughput.
It does not state that native XRP is the bridge asset, settlement principal, collateral or the asset purchased by the participating capital providers.
C2FO and Ripple are counterparties to the same joint announcement; their releases are not independent measurements of production activity.

claims_supported: The current product page still presents a Join Waitlist call to action.
The page says Instant Pay will launch with a limited rollout over the coming months.
The page says availability will be limited to the United States at launch.
The page describes payment within minutes after an approved invoice is confirmed for early payment.
limitations: A product page description and waitlist are not evidence of production deployment, funded transactions or XRPL settlement volume.
The page does not identify capital providers or disclose transaction-level settlement data.
The public page does not establish that every waitlisted supplier has access.

claims_supported: Ripple's version reports more than $520 billion of working capital accessed through existing C2FO Early Pay programs.
limitations: The figure describes pre-existing Early Pay programs, not new Instant Pay funding or XRPL/RLUSD settlement volume.
C2FO's own release says more than $525 billion; the two rounded statements are preserved as a $5 billion source discrepancy and are not averaged.
The difference may reflect rounding or differing reporting cutoffs; the public extracts do not resolve the methodology.

relationships.rollout_statement: Limited rollout over the coming months

actual_capital_classification.historical_early_pay_scope: Existing Early Pay programs; not Instant Pay and not XRPL/RLUSD settlement volume.
actual_capital_classification.discrepancy_usd: 5000000000 between the rounded lower-bound claims; methodology unresolved.
actual_capital_classification.rule: Do not classify a waitlist, announced funding model, historical program volume, or unquantified custody capability as new actual capital deployed.

competing_hypotheses.claim: C2FO Instant Pay could increase XRPL/RLUSD activity without generating material incremental native XRP spot demand.
support: RLUSD is the named settlement asset.
The product page describes a limited rollout and waitlist.
disconfirming_or_missing: No production XRPL transaction or fee attribution is published.
Any incremental XRP acquired for reserves or fees is unquantified.

competing_hypotheses.claim: BNY's XRP custody capability could reduce institutional custody friction and enable future holdings.
support: BNY explicitly states that its Digital Asset Custody platform supports native XRP for eligible clients.
disconfirming_or_missing: No XRP assets under custody, client count, account openings or purchases are disclosed.
Custody can support existing holdings without changing net demand.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Participating capital providers may deploy actual cash when Instant Pay access expands.
support: C2FO and Ripple describe a funding model using participating capital providers.
disconfirming_or_missing: The product page still shows a waitlist and limited rollout over coming months.
Provider identities, funded amounts and settlement receipts are absent.

disconfirming_evidence: The C2FO product page still presents a waitlist and a limited rollout rather than broad general availability.
The release names RLUSD, not XRP, as the settlement asset.
No funded amount, provider identity, supplier count or transaction volume is disclosed.
BNY's XRP custody capability is not quantified by asset-specific AUC.
The $520B and $525B historical Early Pay figures are not Instant Pay volume.
next_actions: Monitor the C2FO Instant Pay page for a change from waitlist/limited rollout to generally available service.
Seek primary evidence identifying participating capital providers and actual funded invoices.
Verify production XRPL transactions and RLUSD settlement volumes separately from XRP bridge usage.
Seek BNY asset-specific XRP custody balances or other independently quantified institutional holdings.
Preserve the $520B/$525B Early Pay source difference until methodology and cutoff are reconciled.
Capture original source bytes, SHA-256 receipts and independent timestamps before model admission.
